name: AspireUI
description: Self-hosted app platform and visual builder: install apps from a built-in store of 160+, deploy any docker-compose repository straight from Git, and manage everything that runs — logs, env vars, ports, volumes, backups and domains. Also a visual editor for .NET Aspire AppHost projects.
longDescription:
AspireUI turns a server into a self-hosted app platform. Its built-in store carries 160+ ready-to-run apps, and anything else can be installed straight from a Git repository that has a docker-compose.yml — no manual file editing.

Everything it starts stays managed: start, stop, update and restart, live CPU and memory, container health that tells a crash-looping app from a healthy one, log streaming, an environment-variable and port editor, a volume file browser, a one-shot repair terminal for containers that will not stay up, scheduled volume backups with restore, notifications via webhook or Telegram, and your own domains with Let's Encrypt HTTPS.

It is also a visual editor for .NET Aspire AppHost projects: drag resources onto a canvas, get real C# code, run the stack, or publish it as Docker Compose, a Helm chart or Azure Bicep. Apps can be deployed to this machine, to another box over SSH, to a Kubernetes cluster or to a managed container platform — and moved between them together with their data.

Host access: AspireUI mounts the Docker socket, because starting and hosting other containers is what it does. That is root-equivalent access to this server; install it only if you want AspireUI to control Docker here.

A setup wizard creates the admin account on first start.
